approachQuestion.prompt:
Retain Future Benchmarks

A finite acyclic singly linked list contains integer scores. Remove a node exactly when some strictly greater score occurs later in the original chain. Return the retained original nodes in original order; equal later scores do not remove a node. Preserve all values and change only next links. Removed nodes need not be cleared. Input is head; 0 <= n <= 200000; scores are signed 32-bit integers.

Input: [5,2,8,8,3,6]. Output: [8,8,6].
Input: [4,4,4]. Output: all three original nodes in original order.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Iteratively reverse the list. Walk it while maintaining the greatest score seen, keeping a node exactly when its score is at least that maximum. Bypass other nodes, then iteratively reverse the retained chain and return its head.
options.feedback: In reversed order, already seen nodes are precisely the original later nodes. The strict-removal rule becomes a greater-than-or-equal keep test.

options.text: Copy all node references into an array. Scan it right to left with a running maximum, collect the retained references, then relink those references in original order.
options.feedback: This applies the correct suffix criterion, but the arrays are avoidable when temporary reversal is allowed.

options.text: Scan left to right and keep only scores at least as large as all previously seen scores.
options.feedback: For [5,2,8], this keeps 5 even though later 8 must remove it; it checks the wrong side.

options.text: Reverse, keep only scores strictly greater than the running maximum, then reverse the survivors.
options.feedback: For [4,4,4] this keeps only one node, but equal later values must not remove earlier nodes.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-20-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: Two iterative reversals and one maximum scan each visit at most n nodes. Every score must be considered in the worst case, so time is linear. Only fixed references and a maximum value are stored, with null naturally producing an empty retained chain; all output nodes are supplied, with no arrays or recursive calls.
